name: Familial Syringomyelia

criteria.description: Presence of progressive sensory dissociation with loss of pain and temperature sensation in a cape-like distribution
MRI evidence of a syrinx or cystic cavity within the spinal cord
Documented family history of syringomyelia or related spinal cord cystic lesions
Presence of muscle weakness or atrophy in upper limbs
Hyporeflexia or areflexia in affected segments

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of MRI-confirmed syrinx plus clinical symptoms consistent with syringomyelia and a positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be supportive but is not yet standardized for diagnosis.

imaging: MRI showing fluid-filled syrinx within spinal cord
Possible associated Chiari malformation on brain MRI
genetic: Familial inheritance pattern suggesting autosomal dominant or recessive transmission
No specific gene identified; genetic testing currently investigational
other: Electrophysiological studies may show segmental denervation

distinguishingFeatures: Structural hindbrain herniation visible on MRI
Often associated with syringomyelia but distinct anatomical findings
History of trauma, infection, or tumor causing syrinx formation
